marching in place (standing):
    Setup: Stand tall with your feet under your hips and your arms loose.
    Cues: Lift one knee, then the other, at an easy rhythm. Swing the opposite arm. Land softly and quietly.
    Rep: March at an easy, steady rhythm for the whole time. It should feel like a brisk walk, and you can talk in full sentences.
    Feel: Feel the legs warming up and the heart rate rising a little, with no strain in the knees, hips or back.
    Faults: If you slump, stand tall and let the opposite arm swing. If your steps get heavy, lift the knees only as high as feels easy and land softly. If you are out of breath, slow the pace until you can chat easily.
    Easier: seated march
    Harder: high knees
  push-up (all-fours):
    Setup: Hands under your shoulders, body in one long line from head to heels, or from head to knees.
    Cues: Push the floor away. Ribs down, glutes tight. Elbows at a gentle angle, not flared.
    Rep: One rep is lowering your chest toward the floor and pressing back up to straight arms.
    Feel: Feel it in the chest, the fronts of the shoulders and the backs of the arms, with your core tight and no sag in the low back.
    Faults: If your hips sag, squeeze the glutes and brace your belly. If your elbows flare wide, tuck them to a gentle angle. If you only go halfway, lower your chest a little closer to the floor.
    Easier: incline push-up
    Harder: weighted vest push-up, handle push-up
  lateral lunge (standing, one side at a time):
    Setup: Stand tall, feet together, hands at your chest or holding light weights at your sides.
    Cues: Step wide to one side, toes forward. Sit back into that hip, the far leg long. Push off and pull back to the middle.
    Rep: One rep is a wide step to the side, sitting back into the bent leg with the far leg straight, then pushing back to the middle. Count reps on each side.
    Feel: Feel it in the bent leg's thigh and glute and along the inner thigh of the straight leg, with no pinch in the knee or the groin.
    Faults: If you feel a sharp pull high in the inner thigh, take a shorter step and sit less deep. If the bent knee caves in, point it over the middle of your foot. If the heel of the bent leg lifts, sit back more and keep the whole foot down.
    Easier: sumo squat
    Harder: cossack squat
  glute bridge (lying):
    Setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip width apart.
    Cues: Ribs down, then lift the hips. Squeeze the glutes at the top and hold one beat. Lower one notch at a time.
    Rep: One rep is lifting your hips until your body makes a straight line from knees to shoulders, then lowering back down.
    Feel: Feel it in the back of the hips and the hamstrings, not the low back.
    Faults: If your low back arches, tuck your ribs down and stop the lift sooner. If you feel it in the hamstrings only, pull your heels a little closer. If your knees drift apart, keep them hip width.
    Harder: single-leg glute bridge, dumbbell glute bridge, hip thrust
  prone y t w raise (lying):
    Setup: Lie face down, forehead resting on a folded towel or your hands, arms long.
    Cues: Lift the arms in a Y, then a T, then a W. Thumbs up, shoulders away from your ears. Small and slow, no weight needed.
    Rep: One rep is a Y, then a T, then a W, lifting and lowering each one. All three together count as one rep.
    Feel: Feel it in the upper back between the shoulder blades, not in the neck or the low back.
    Faults: If your neck strains, keep your forehead resting and look at the floor. If you shrug, slide your shoulders away from your ears. If your low back arches, keep your legs and belly relaxed and lift only the arms.
  forearm plank (all-fours):
    Setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders, legs long behind you, or knees down for an easier version.
    Cues: Squeeze the glutes. Ribs down, long line from head to heels. Breathe steadily.
    Rep: Hold the straight line from head to heels, or head to knees. The hold ends when your hips sag or your low back starts to ache.
    Feel: Feel it in the belly, the glutes and the front of the shoulders, not as a pinch in the low back.
    Faults: If your hips sag, squeeze the glutes and pull your ribs down toward your hips. If your hips pike up high, lower them until your body is one long line. If your shoulders sink between the arms, press the forearms into the floor and push the floor away.
  figure-four stretch (lying, one side at a time):
    Setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
    Cues: Reach through and hold behind the bottom thigh. Draw it gently toward you. Keep the crossed foot flexed.
    Rep: Hold the crossed leg drawn toward you. The hold ends when the time is up, then switch sides.
    Feel: Feel a mild stretch deep in the glute of the crossed leg, and no pinch in the knee.
    Faults: If the knee feels sore, keep the crossed foot flexed and ease the pull. If your head and shoulders lift, rest them down and relax the neck. If you pull hard, draw the leg gently until you feel mild tension.
  belly breathing (seated):
    Setup: Sit tall with one hand on your chest and one on your belly.
    Cues: Breathe in and let the belly rise. The chest hand stays still. Breathe out slowly and let it fall.
    Rep: One cycle is a slow breath in as the belly rises, then a slow breath out as it falls.
    Feel: Feel the belly hand rise and fall while the chest hand stays almost still.
    Faults: If the chest hand moves first, slow down and send the breath lower. If you strain or gulp air, make the breath smaller and softer. If you feel dizzy, breathe normally for a moment.
